# ANPR2MQTT

> Simple camera integration using file system and MQTT, specialising in ANPR

ANPR2MQTT watches a camera's exported snapshot/event files (or an FTP or MQTT feed), runs OCR locally where needed, and publishes structured MQTT messages and images for Home Assistant auto-discovery.


# Usage

# anpr2mqtt

# ANPR MQTT Bridge

A simple way to integrate into Home Assistant (or other MQTT consumers) any CCTV camera that can upload files via FTP, NAS etc into a monitored directory. Specializes in **ANPR** (**Automatic Number Plate Recognition**, aka **ALPR** or **Automatic License Plate Recognition**) with support for face events, and configurable for other event types. Running under Docker is preferred but not necessary.

All that is needed is for the camera to be configured to upload images on plate recognition, or any other event, by ftp, NAS or whatever else. ANPR2MQTT monitors the directory where the images lands and publishes plate, or other event, information to MQTT. Its simple, requires no proprietary vendor APIs ( or differing ONVIF implementations ), and Home Assistant gets a copy of the actual annotated detection image to use on dashboards or to attach to notifications.

While it specialises in vehicle plate detection, it can watch for any camera event that uploads images, such as face capture, scene change, missing object, unattended baggage or line crossing, defined by configuration alone, without `anpr2mqtt` needing to know about each one. See [Other Events](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk/camera/#other-events). A single `anpr2mqtt` instance can watch multiple paths and patterns for different cameras and events.

Info

The enrichment features, such as DVLA lookup and previous sightings, are now integrated directly into the Home Assistant Marketplace integration [Camera AutoNotify](https://camera-autonotify.rhizomatics.org.uk) and this is now the recommended method, and with this integration there is no longer any reason to divert Frigate messages via `anpr2mqtt`.

The functionality can still be used in `anpr2mqtt`, which may be needed if transitioning to AutoNotify or using something or than Home Assistant. There is also an import function in AutoNotify to pull in previous sightings and plate classifications from `anpr2mqtt` configuration.

## Features

- **Minimal configuration**
  - Ready configured to work with popular Hikvision ANPR camera settings
  - See [Example Camera Configuration](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk/camera/index.md)
- **File System Integration**
  - Watches directory for camera images using [Watchdog](https://python-watchdog.readthedocs.io/en/stable/index.html)
    - Uses [inotify](https://www.man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/inotify.7.html) on Linux, or equiv on other operating systems for efficient listening to file system events without continual polling
  - Extracts target ( for example licence plate ), timestamp and event type information from filenames
- **[Other Camera Events](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk/camera/#other-events)**
  - Face capture, scene change, line crossing, region entry or any other event a camera uploads images for, by configuration
  - Kept apart from plates, with no plate lookups or corrections
  - Paired images, such as a face crop and its whole scene, as one event
  - Minimum gap between events, for noisy or repeating events
- **[Home Assistant Integration](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk/homeassistant/index.md)**
  - Publishes plates to MQTT for Home Assistant as a [MQTT Sensor Entity](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sensor.mqtt/), and other events as a [MQTT Event Entity](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/event.mqtt/)
  - [Image counts](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk/homeassistant/#image-counts) per event, for today, this week and in total, for health checks such as a camera that's stopped sending images
  - [Upload monitoring](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk/camera/#uploads) of an ftp landing zone, counting every file that arrives, as a sensor that doesn't notify
  - Auto-discovery configuration for Home Assistant
  - Creates [MQTT Image Entity](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/image.mqtt/) on Home Assistant for image snapshot, so no web access to ftp needed
  - Optionally also creates an [MQTT Camera Entity](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/camera.mqtt/)
- **Integrated OCR** (Text Recognition)
  - OCR-based extraction of fields using [tesseract-ocr](https://github.com/tesseract-ocr/tesseract)
    - By default direction detection (*Forward*/*Reverse*) for example as stamped on an image by a Hikvision ANPR camera
    - Corrections by regular expression to fix OCR mis-readings
- Plate Enrichment
  - Tracks and counts previous sightings
  - Configurable to classify plates as known, to be ignored or as a potential threat
  - Regular expression based corrections, for known plates that the ANPR sometimes mis-reads
  - Fuzzy match corrections for known plates, based on Levenshtein algorithm
  - UK Only
    - [DVLA Lookup](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk/api/index.md) if API_KEY provided, for detailed MOT and tax information
    - Lookups cached for configurable time
  - For Home Assistant, [Camera AutoNotify](https://camera-autonotify.rhizomatics.org.uk) is recommended to do this rather than in anpr2mqtt.
- Frigate Integration
  - All the same enrichments, including DVLA lookup, can also be extended to licence plates recognized by Frigate ( see [Frigate License Plate Recognition](https://docs.frigate.video/configuration/license_plate_recognition)), assuming that `frigate/events` and `frigate/tracked_object_update` topics are on the same MQTT broker.
  - Shares same sighting tracking as local images
  - For Home Assistant, [Camera AutoNotify](https://camera-autonotify.rhizomatics.org.uk) is recommended to do this rather than in anpr2mqtt.
- Auto clear vehicle state optionally, after configurable time
- [Debug Tools](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk/debug_tools/index.md) built-in

## Container Deployment

Build and run with Docker or Podman, example [docker-compose.yaml](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk/examples/docker_compose/index.md) provided.

## Configuration

ANPR2MQTT uses [pydantic-settings](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/pydantic_settings/), which means configuration can happen in a variety of ways, and these can be combined - yaml configuration file, environment variables, Docker Secrets, built-in defaults, and `.env` file or command line arguments.

Camera names, and each event's `event`, `camera` and `target_type`, are used in MQTT topics, Home Assistant entity ids and file names, so they must be 1 to 64 letters, digits, `_` or `-`, such as `front_door`. Anything else, such as a space, `/`, `.`, `+` or `#`, stops `anpr2mqtt` starting, with a message saying which one. Use `description` for text to show in Home Assistant.

### CLI Arguments

Every configuration setting can be passed as a command line argument, using dot notation for nested settings. This is the highest-priority source and overrides all other configuration.

```bash
uvx anpr2mqtt --mqtt.host 192.168.1.10 --mqtt.port 1884 --log_level DEBUG
```

Run `uvx anpr2mqtt --help` to see all available flags, and find more information at [Debug Tools](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk/debug_tools/index.md)

When running outside Docker, OCR also needs the `tesseract` binary installed, e.g. `brew install tesseract` on macOS.

## Home Assistant Integration

See [Home Assistant Integration](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk/homeassistant/index.md) for configuration and example notification automation.

### Environment Variables

[pydantic-settings](https://docs.pydantic.dev/latest/concepts/pydantic_settings/) needs double underscores for environment variables in config sections. For example, `MQTT__HOST` means set the value `host` in the `mqtt` config section.

| Env Variable       | Description                | Default     |
| ------------------ | -------------------------- | ----------- |
| `MQTT__HOST`       | MQTT broker hostname       | `localhost` |
| `MQTT__PORT`       | MQTT broker port           | `1883`      |
| `MQTT__TOPIC_ROOT` | MQTT topic for events      | `anpr2mqtt` |
| `MQTT__USER`       | MQTT username              | -           |
| `MQTT__PASS`       | MQTT password              | -           |
| `LOG_LEVEL`        | Python logging level       | INFO        |
| `DVLA__API_KEY`    | API Key for Gov API Lookup | -           |

## Image Filename Format

Expected format: `YYYYMMDDHHMMSSmmm_PLATE_VEHICLE_DETECTION.jpg`

Example: `20180502174029596_A2GEO_VEHICLE_DETECTION.jpg`

Each event should say what it's for with `target_type`, `plate` for ANPR, or anything else for other events. Leaving it out means `plate`, so older configurations still work, but any event without it becomes a plate event, with a plate sensor, even on a camera with no ANPR.

A regular expression can be defined to match different file name formats, such as for other events, `10.180.10.30_01_20261127071024588_SCENE_CHANGE_DETECTION.jpg`, see [Other Events](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk/camera/#other-events).

## Image Box Coordinates

Where cameras provide an estimated direction for the vehicle, this can be captured via OCR and included in the response. See [OCR](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk/ocr/index.md) for an explanation and examples.

## Auto Clear

By default, the state will be reset back to unavailable 5 minutes after a detection, while the image will be left present as record of last known vehicle. This behavior can be changed ( to switch off auto clear, or change the time lag, or also clear image ) using the `autoclear` configuration for each event.

configuration snippet

```yaml
- camera: shed
  target_type: plate
  watch_path: /ftp/shedcam
  autoclear:
    post_event: 360
    state: True
    image: False
```

## Corrections

The licence plate detection may mis-read or miss some of the characters of the plate. When the result is published to MQTT, both the raw original and corrected versions are provided.

Two mechanisms help with this:

### Fuzzy Matching

The Levenshtein method is used to compare the plate against a list of known plates in the configuration, subject to a maximum distance tolerance ( number of mismatched characters ) defined by `auto_match_tolerance` for the event. If its a match for more than one, the plate with least distance is chosen.

### Regex / String Matching

Each known plate can be associated with a list of regular expressions and/or plain strings, and these will be checked for every discovered licence plate.

### Working with Frigate

A Frigate camera's plates are published as the camera of the same name in the `cameras` config. Where the namesdiffer, link the camera to the Frigate camera by name in `linked_cameras`:

```yaml
cameras:
- name: drive
  linked_cameras:
    frigate: driveway_lpr
    unifiprotect: Driveway G4
```

`linked_cameras` can also name the same camera in any other integration that sees it, such as UniFi Protect, Viseron or Blue Iris, each keyed by its Home Assistant domain, `unifiprotect`, `viseron` or `blueiris`. They're given to Home Assistant as the `linked_cameras` attribute, along with the Frigate camera matched by name, for integrations that join anpr2mqtt sightings to the events of the cameras they supplement.

## Primary Dependencies

- **watchdog** - File system monitoring (cross-platform)
- **paho-mqtt** - MQTT client
- **Pillow** - Image processing
- **pytesseract** - OCR for direction detection
- **structlog** - Structured logging
- **niquests** - API Client
- **niquests-cache** - API result caching

Also available on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/updates2mqtt/)

# Camera Configuration

Any camera that can upload an image for an event, by ftp, to a NAS or otherwise, with a timestamp in its file name, can be used with `anpr2mqtt`. ANPR is its speciality, so the Hikvision ANPR camera below is the main example, followed by [Other Events](#other-events), such as face capture and scene change, from the same or other cameras.

## Hikvision

### Example

This example uses the [DS-2CD4A25FWD-IZS](https://specsheets.dvs.co.uk/DS-2CD4A25FWD-IZS.pdf), one of the very first ANPR enabled Hikvision cameras, on its own, without any NVR.

ANPR configuration, including posting images via ftp, is configured in the *Road Traffic* menu under *Advanced*.

At the bottom of the page is the configuration for actions upon detecting a plate.

The server name, user name and password, and upload directory for this ftp are set once for all ftp actions in the *Network* menu under *Advanced Configuration*.

Some of the results of the recognition algorithm are available either on the picture and/or as part of the image file name. Direction is one that's only available with this model on the image. Its also possible to play with text colour here, although `anpr2mqtt` will optionally invert the colours pre-scan, so its possible to leave it as white text on black background to be clearer for humans to read.

The file name format is configurable, it should have the licence plate included and the timestamp to work with the default `anpr2mqtt` regular expression. There's no need to include camera number if there's only one ANPR camera.

### Image Settings

The Hikvision camera has a special set of image settings bundled as a **Mounting Scenario**

One side-effect of this is that the camera can be practically useless as a general purpose CCTV camera in anything other than very bright conditions if the *Road* Mounting Scenario is chosen.

One way of coping with this is to switch between mount scenarios, so its *Normal* at day time and *Road* at night, or have it on *Road* only when there is heightened security need.

#### Home Assistant Automated Mount Scenario Change

Set up two REST commands, changing `192.168.1.100` for the IP address or host name of your own camera, and adding `hik_user` and `hik_password` values to the `secrets.yaml` file (see [Storing Secrets](https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/configuration/secrets/)).

REST Command Definitions

```text
driveway_cam_road:
    url: http://192.168.1.100/ISAPI/Image/channels/1/mountingScenario
    method: put
    content_type: text/xml
    username: !secret hik_user
    password: !secret hik_password
    payload: '<MountingScenario xmlns="http://www.hikvision.com/ver20/XMLSchema" version="2.0"><mode>road</mode></MountingScenario>'

driveway_cam_normal:
    url: http://192.168.1.100/ISAPI/Image/channels/1/mountingScenario
    method: put
    content_type: text/xml
    username: !secret hik_user
    password: !secret hik_password
    payload: '<MountingScenario xmlns="http://www.hikvision.com/ver20/XMLSchema" version="2.0"><mode>normal</mode></MountingScenario>'
```

These commands can now be used in Home Assistant automations as actions, triggered by time of day, state of sun etc.

## Other Events

Hikvision cameras have many other events besides ANPR, such as face capture, scene change, line crossing, region entry or unattended baggage, and can ftp images for any of them. Any of these can be added as an event, so long as the camera puts a timestamp in the file name, without anpr2mqtt having to know about each one.

As with ANPR, the file name format is set on the camera. For example, from camera IP address, channel and timestamp, then the event's own name:

- `10.180.10.30_01_20261127071024588_SCENE_CHANGE_DETECTION.jpg`
- `10.180.10.40_01_20261125175413139_FACE_DETECTION.jpg`

Every event should have a `target_type`, `plate` for ANPR, and anything else for other events, along with an `image_name_re` matching its file names ( `target_type` defaults to `plate`, for compatibility with older configurations). It can be on the same camera as an ANPR event, and share the same `watch_path`, since each event only picks up files matching its own `image_name_re`.

```yaml
events:
- camera: shed
  event: anpr
  target_type: plate
  watch_path: /ftp/Shed
- camera: shed
  event: scene_change
  target_type: scene_change
  watch_path: /ftp/Shed
  image_name_re: (?P<ip>[0-9.]+)_(?P<channel>[0-9]+)_(?P<dt>[0-9]{17})_(?P<event>SCENE_CHANGE_DETECTION)\.(?P<ext>jpg|png|gif|jpeg)
  min_event_gap_seconds: 60
  ocr_field_ids: []
```

These events are kept apart from plates:

- **Home Assistant** gets an [event entity](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/event/), such as `event.scene_change_shed`, rather than a sensor, on the same device as the camera's ANPR sensor. Its `event_type` is the event's name, here `scene_change`, with the usual [attributes](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk/homeassistant/#attributes). There's also an image entity and a camera entity, as for ANPR
- **Integrations that take an anpr2mqtt device's sensors as plates**, such as [Camera AutoNotify](https://camera-autonotify.rhizomatics.org.uk), don't see them
- **No plate handling**: no DVLA lookup, plate correction or Frigate licence plates
- **Defaults**: none of the plate defaults. `event` is the `target_type`, so `event: scene_change` above could be left out, rather than `anpr`. `default_description` comes from the event name, here `Scene change`, rather than `Unknown vehicle`. `icon` is `mdi:cctv` rather than `mdi:car-back`. There's no OCR, rather than the Hikvision vehicle direction, so `ocr_field_ids: []` isn't needed

There's usually no `target` in these file names, so nothing to look up, correct or track, and the event entity records when each was seen. Where a camera sends several images a second or so apart for the same thing, `min_event_gap_seconds` makes them one event, publishing only the first within that many seconds of the last.

### Face Capture

Some cameras send two images per face: a `FACE_SNAP` cropped to the face, and a `FACE_BACKGROUND` of the whole scene, a few milliseconds later, such as `10.180.10.20_01_20261120175018129_FACE_SNAP.jpg`. With `secondary_image_event`, the `FACE_BACKGROUND` is published as a second image entity, such as `image.face_driveway_face_background`, rather than as another event, so there's one event per face, with the `FACE_SNAP` as its image.

```yaml
- camera: driveway
  event: face
  target_type: face
  default_description: Face
  icon: mdi:face-recognition
  watch_path: /ftp/Driveway
  image_name_re: (?P<ip>[0-9.]+)_(?P<channel>[0-9]+)_(?P<dt>[0-9]{17})_(?P<event>FACE_SNAP|FACE_BACKGROUND)\.(?P<ext>jpg|png|gif|jpeg)
  secondary_image_event: FACE_BACKGROUND
  ocr_field_ids: []
```

Other cameras send only one image per face, `FACE_DETECTION`, often several a second or so apart. Match that event name, leave out `secondary_image_event`, and set `min_event_gap_seconds`, such as `10`.

## Uploads

An event with `target_type: upload` counts every file arriving in, or removed from, its `watch_path`, and the files there now, without looking inside them, so they don't need a timestamp in the file name, or even to be images. Nothing is published for each file, so nothing is notified, only a Home Assistant sensor of when the last file arrived, such as `sensor.upload_shed`, with its counts.

It can be used on its own, as a general purpose monitor of an ftp landing zone, or alongside a directory's other events, to check there's been some activity, such as scene changes or snapshots, even when no plates have arrived.

Uploads aren't tied to a camera, since several cameras may share one landing zone, or one camera upload to several, so `camera` isn't needed. Each upload is told apart by its `id` instead, which can be left out if there's only one.

```yaml
events:
- target_type: upload
  id: shed
  watch_path: /ftp/Shed
- target_type: upload
  id: all
  description: All ftp uploads
  watch_path: /ftp
  watch_tree: true
```

The sensor's state is the time the last file arrived, with attributes:

```yaml
event: upload
id: all
watch_path: /ftp
# files there now
current: 2210
current_bytes: 1385402880
# files arrived
today: 41
today_bytes: 25690112
this_week: 230
this_week_bytes: 144179200
total: 9120
total_bytes: 5716836352
last_received: "2026-11-27T08:02:11.120000+00:00"
last_file: Shed/10.180.10.30_01_20261127080211120_SCENE_CHANGE_DETECTION.jpg
# files removed
removed_today: 0
removed_today_bytes: 0
removed_this_week: 1850
removed_this_week_bytes: 1159725056
removed_total: 6910
removed_total_bytes: 4331433472
last_removed: "2026-11-24T03:00:02.501000+00:00"
last_removed_file: Shed/10.180.10.30_01_20261117061533114_SCENE_CHANGE_DETECTION.jpg
```

- **Current**: the files in the `watch_path` now, found by a scan at startup, kept up to date as files arrive and are removed, and scanned again each midnight. Arrivals and removals only count from when `anpr2mqtt` started watching, so with files coming and going, such as a camera or NAS clearing out old images, it's `current` that says what's there
- **Arrivals**: counted when a file is closed after being written, as an ftp upload is, or renamed to a matching name, such as from an ftp server's temporary upload name. A file moved in whole from elsewhere is in `current`, but not counted as an arrival
- **Removals**: a file deleted, moved out of the `watch_path`, or renamed to a name that no longer matches. Sizes are as last seen, since the file has gone
- **Which files**: any file by default, or only those matching `image_name_re`, such as `.*\.jpg`, which needs no `dt` group for an upload. With `watch_tree: true`, files in subdirectories count too, and `last_file` is relative to the `watch_path`
- **Naming**: the sensor is `sensor.upload_<id>`, such as `sensor.upload_all` above, or `sensor.upload` without an `id`. Each upload needs its own `id`, checked at startup. `id` is only for uploads, other events are told apart by `event` and `camera`
- **Camera**: optional, and if given, only shown as a `camera` attribute, such as for a camera's own landing zone
- **No device**: the sensor isn't on any `anpr2mqtt` device, as for the [individual or group sensors](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk/homeassistant/#individual-or-group-sensors), so integrations that take an anpr2mqtt device's sensors as plates, such as [Camera AutoNotify](https://camera-autonotify.rhizomatics.org.uk), don't see it
- **Nothing else**: no image, camera or event entity, OCR, tracking or autoclear
- **Counts**: as for [image counts](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk/homeassistant/#image-counts), kept across restarts and back to 0 at midnight, with sizes in bytes

- Home Assistant built-in [Hikvision Integration](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/hikvision/)
  - Has support for 'Surveillance Center' notifications but with open [issue #115631](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/115631) for ANPR integration.

# OCR

Any number of textual fields can be scanned from the image. By default this happens for `vehicle_direction` as in this Hikvision example.

Each field can have optional permitted values (`Unknown` returned if none of them found) and a set of corrections to handle occasional OCR errors, where corrections are simple strings or regular expressions.

Use the [OCR Tool](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk/debug_tools/#ocr-ocr_file) for quick tests of configuration with a local image

## OCR Stages

1. Crop the image to a box starting at `x` and `y` position, measured from the bottom left of the image and a given height and width
1. Optionally invert the image colours for better capture accuracy
1. Run OCR over the cropped image
1. Apply optional corrections
1. Optionally restrict to a list of values, forcing case if needed

## Startup Check

When any event uses OCR fields, ANPR2MQTT reads a small bundled sample image at startup, the caption bar from the Hikvision example above, and expects `vehicle_direction` to be `Forward`. This checks the [Tesseract](https://github.com/tesseract-ocr/tesseract) OCR engine is installed and working, independently of your own field settings, and logs either `Verified OCR` or an error. The app keeps running either way, but OCR fields will read as `Unknown` until a failure is fixed.

Outside Docker, a failure usually means the `tesseract` binary isn't installed or isn't on the `PATH`. Every event reads the `hik_direction` field unless told otherwise, so if your images have no text worth reading, turn OCR off for each event with `ocr_field_ids: []`. That also skips this check. To skip only the check:

```yaml
ocr:
  verify_on_startup: false
```

## Example Configuration

The configuration for this can be in the `anpr2mqtt.yaml` file, or in environment variables or command line arguments.

In this example `hik_direction` is the `ocr_field_id` value that can be referenced in an event, and `label` is the name of the attribute that will appear in the Home Asssitant entity attributes.

```yaml
ocr:
  hik_direction:
    label: vehicle_direction
    values: Reverse, Forward
    invert: true
    crop: 
      x: 0
      y: 850
      h: 30
      w: 650
    correction:
      Forward:
      - F.*wd
      Reverse:
      - R.*v.*se
      - Back.*
```

Use the [debug tools](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk/debug_tools/index.md) to quickly iterate over an image, for example:

```bash
uvx --from anpr2mqtt anprtools ocr_file 20260130174327627_K39ZTB_VEHICLE_DETECTION.jpg
```

or to test cropping values:

```bash
uvx --from anpr2mqtt anprtools ocr_file example_image.jpg \
  --ocr.crop.x 850 --ocr.crop.y 0 --ocr.crop.h 200 --ocr.crop.w 400
```

# HomeAssistant Integration

`anpr2mqtt` represents each ANPR cameras as a [MQTT Sensor](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sensor.mqtt/) and [MQTT Image](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/image.mqtt/) entities, and uses [MQTT discovery](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/mqtt/#mqtt-discovery) so that HomeAssistant automatically picks up components discovered by ANPR2MQTT with zero configuration on HomeAssistant itself.

The MQTT image entity can be used in the same way as a `camera` entity, so can be included in mobile push, email etc notifications, or added to a Home Assistant dashboard. See the example below, or use [Supernotify](https://supernotify.rhizomatics.org.uk) camera support.

## Auto Notify

Use [Camera AutoNotify](https://camera-autonotify.rhizomatics.org.uk) to automatically set up notifications with **zero YAML** and **no automations** required. It will also do plate enrichment, such as by tracking previous sightings, corrections, ignoring, classifying as known, prioritizing based on plate and UK DVLA lookup.

## Attributes

Both the `sensor` and `image` attributes have the same extensive set of attributes. For events other than plates, the event entity has them too, with `event_type` as the event's name, all from the event itself, so they're always those of the event that changed its state, apart from [image counts](#image-counts), which are refreshed between events.

The target value will also appear in a field named after `target_type`, for example, `plate` for easier to read Home Assistant automations.

| Attribute                  | Example                                                                                |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| target                     | J23TST                                                                                 |
| target_type                | plate                                                                                  |
| `target_type`              | J23TST                                                                                 |
| source                     | filesystem                                                                             |
| reg_info                   | null                                                                                   |
| area                       | driveway                                                                               |
| camera                     | drivewacam                                                                             |
| linked_cameras             | `{"frigate": "driveway"}`, the same camera in other integrations, by domain            |
| orig_target                | J23TST                                                                                 |
| ignore                     | false                                                                                  |
| known                      | true                                                                                   |
| dangerous                  | false                                                                                  |
| priority                   | medium                                                                                 |
| description                | Amazon Prime                                                                           |
| history.previous_sightings | 15                                                                                     |
| history.last_seen          | 2026-01-08T14:15:28.000319+00:00                                                       |
| event_time                 | 2026-01-08T14:15:28.000320+00:00                                                       |
| event_image_url            | http://192.168.10.10/cctv//ftp/Driveway/20260108141528320_J23TST_VEHICLE_DETECTION.jpg |
| image_event                | VEHICLE DETECTION                                                                      |
| ext                        | jpg                                                                                    |
| image_size                 | 124907                                                                                 |

The `reg_info` will be populated with the licence plate API lookup, for example UK DVLA, if provided.

Some attributes are only present for events from a particular source, since they don't apply to the other. `source` is always `filesystem` or `frigate`, and can be used to tell which set to expect:

| Attribute         | Source                                | Example                                                      |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| file_path         | filesystem                            | /ftp/Driveway/20260108141528320_J23TST_VEHICLE_DETECTION.jpg |
| vehicle_direction | filesystem (OCR field, if configured) | Forward                                                      |
| frigate_event_id  | frigate                               | 1790171055.400738-28axk4                                     |
| frigate_ui_url    | frigate                               | http://192.168.10.10:5000/events?id=1790171055.400738-28axk4 |
| frigate           | frigate                               | `{"recognized_license_plate_score": 0.92}`                   |

`event_image_url` is populated for both sources, pointing directly at the event image (the filesystem image on the local web server, or the Frigate event snapshot API), so notification automations can rely on it regardless of which source raised the event.

## Example Automation

This example uses [Supernotify](https://supernotify.rhizomatics.org.uk) to generate multiple alerts, such as email with ANPR image attachment, mobile push with the image and click through to Frigate page, voice assistant announcement and sounding chimes. It can also be used with any of the built-in notification integrations, though without the same multiple-transport and media handling capabilities.

```yaml
alias: Driveway ANPR Alert
description: Notify via email, chime, Alexa and mobile push when a vehicle identified
triggers:
  - trigger: state
    entity_id:
      - sensor.anpr_driveway
    attribute: event_time
conditions:
  - condition: not
    conditions:
      - condition: state
        entity_id: sensor.anpr_driveway
        state:
          - unavailable
          - unknown
actions:
  - action: notify.supernotifier
    metadata: {}
    data:
      message: >-
        {{ trigger.to_state.attributes.description }} with {{
        trigger.to_state.attributes.plate }} spotted at {{
        trigger.to_state.attributes.camera }} camera{% if
        trigger.to_state.attributes.vehicle_direction is defined %}, moving {{
        trigger.to_state.attributes.vehicle_direction }}{% endif %}

        {% if trigger.to_state.attributes.history.previous_sightings == 0 %} Not
        previously sighted  {% else %}  with {{
        trigger.to_state.attributes.history.previous_sightings }} previous
        sightings. {% endif %} {% if
        trigger.to_state.attributes.history.last_seen is defined and
        trigger.to_state.attributes.history.last_seen is not none %} last
        seen on {{ trigger.to_state.attributes.history.last_seen[:10] }} at
        {{ trigger.to_state.attributes.history.last_seen[11:16] }}   {%
        endif %}

        {% if 'reg_info' in trigger.to_state.attributes and
        trigger.to_state.attributes.reg_info is not none %}  DVLA info: {{
        trigger.to_state.attributes.reg_info }}   {% endif %}

        {% if 'hourly_counts' in trigger.to_state.attributes.history and
        trigger.to_state.attributes.history.hourly_counts is not none %}  Visit
        History: {% for time,count in
        trigger.to_state.attributes.history.hourly_counts.items() %}
          {{ time }}{% if int(time) < 12 %}am{% else %}pm{% endif %} : {{ count }} times
        {% endfor %}{% endif %}
      title: >-
        {{ trigger.to_state.attributes.description }} spotted on {{
        trigger.to_state.attributes.camera }} camera
      data:
        priority: "{{ trigger.to_state.attributes.priority }}"
        spoken_message: >-
          {{ trigger.to_state.attributes.description }} with {{
          trigger.to_state.attributes.plate }} spotted at {{
          trigger.to_state.attributes.camera }} camera{% if
          trigger.to_state.attributes.vehicle_direction is defined %}, moving {{
          trigger.to_state.attributes.vehicle_direction }}{% endif %}
        apply_scenarios: >-
          {% if trigger.to_state.attributes.known %}known_vehicle{% else
          %}unknown_vehicle{% endif %}
        constrain_scenarios:
          - known_vehicle
          - unknown_vehicle
        media:
          camera_entity_id: image.anpr_{{trigger.to_state.attributes.camera}}
          snapshot_url: >-
            {% if 'event_image_url' in trigger.to_state.attributes %}{{
            trigger.to_state.attributes.event_image_url }}{% endif %}
mode: single
```

## Configuration

In general, no configuration is needed, if Home Assistant is already running with MQTT, and the defaults haven't been changed.

Make sure `anpr2mqtt` is publishing to the same broker, the [MQTT Integration](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/mqtt/) is installed and automatic discovery is not disabled.

The `homeassistant` default topic prefix matches the default ANPR2MQTT config, if its changed in HomeAssistant, then the ANPR2MQTT config must be changed to match.

## Device Creation

A Home Assistant device will be created for each ANPR2MQTT camera, and Home Assistant will then group the relevant entities together on this device page. Use `device_creation: false` in the `homeassistant` config block if you want to switch off this behaviour.

Every device has manufacturer `Rhizomatics` and model `anpr2mqtt`, so other integrations can tell for certain that it's anpr2mqtt's, and its configuration URL is the camera's `live_url`, where that's an `http` or `https` address.

## MQTT Topics

There are 4 separate types of MQTT topic used for HomeAssisstant integration:

- *Config* to support auto discovery.
  - A topic is created per camera, with a name like `homeassistant/sensor/driveway/anpr/config`.
  - For events other than plates, an `event` entity instead, such as `homeassistant/event/driveway/face/config`, see [Other Events](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk/camera/#other-events)
  - For uploads, a sensor of the last upload, such as `homeassistant/sensor/uploads/upload_shed/config`, with its state at `anpr2mqtt/uploads/upload_shed/state`, see [Uploads](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk/camera/#uploads)
  - Optionally a `image` and `camera` topic can be created
  - The `homeassistant` topic prefix can also be configured.
- *State* to report the last plate seen and attributes, by event name and camera, the event name being `anpr` for plates unless configured otherwise, or the `target_type` for other events, such as `face`
  - `anpr2mqtt/<event>/cameras/<camera>/state`, such as `anpr2mqtt/anpr/cameras/driveway/state`
  - `anpr2mqtt/<event>/cameras/<camera>/image`
  - For events other than plates, `anpr2mqtt/<event>/cameras/<camera>/event`, such as `anpr2mqtt/face/cameras/front/event`, fires the event entity, not retained
  - The `anpr2mqtt` topic root can also be configured, with `mqtt.topic_root`
  - When running more than one `anpr2mqtt` on the same broker, give each its own `mqtt.client_id` as well as its own `mqtt.topic_root`, since the broker disconnects a client when another connects with the same client ID. It defaults to `anpr2mqtt`
- *Availability* to show whether ANPR2MQTT itself is running
  - One topic per ANPR2MQTT instance, `anpr2mqtt/availability`, holding `online` or `offline`
  - See [Availability](#availability) below

## Removing Entities

At startup, `anpr2mqtt` removes any Home Assistant entities it created before but no longer has, such as for an event removed from the configuration, a camera renamed, or the image entity switched off. It looks at the retained discovery messages for its own availability topic only, so other `anpr2mqtt` instances on the same broker, with their own `mqtt.topic_root`, and everything else's discovery are left alone. The removed entities' retained state and image topics are cleared too, unless a current entity still uses them.

It's skipped if any event fails to start, so a configuration error can't remove entities that are still wanted, and can be switched off with `homeassistant.remove_stale_entities: false`. Entities from versions before 1.2.0, which had no availability topic, aren't recognised, and need removing by hand.

## Image Counts

Each event's entities have an `images` attribute counting the images received for that event, to check that cameras are still sending them:

```yaml
images:
  today: 3
  today_bytes: 1204224
  this_week: 17
  this_week_bytes: 6823936
  total: 412
  total_bytes: 165376000
  last_received: "2026-11-27T07:10:34.596000+00:00"
```

Every image matching the event's `image_name_re` is counted, whether or not it's published: duplicates, ignored plates, a face's background image, or images within `min_event_gap_seconds`. When an image isn't published, the last state is republished with the new counts, with the state and `event_time` unchanged, so it isn't taken as a new sighting. Days and weeks are in local time, weeks starting on Monday, and the counts are republished at midnight, so `today` goes back to 0 even for a camera that sends nothing. Counts are kept in `image_stats.json` in the tracker's `data_dir`, so they carry on across restarts. Images from Frigate aren't counted, only those from the file system.

For counts across all of a camera's events, or everything arriving in an ftp directory, add an [upload event](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk/camera/#uploads) watching that directory. Where one directory takes all cameras' uploads, that's an overall count too.

For example, a template binary sensor for a camera that's sent no faces today:

```yaml
template:
  - binary_sensor:
      - name: Barn camera quiet
        device_class: problem
        state: "{{ (state_attr('event.face_barn', 'images') or {}).get('today', 0) == 0 }}"
```

## Availability

ANPR2MQTT publishes whether it is running to a retained availability topic, `<topic_root>/availability`, by default `anpr2mqtt/availability`, and every entity's discovery config points to it as its `availability_topic`.

- `online` is published whenever ANPR2MQTT connects or reconnects to the broker
- `offline` is published when it shuts down cleanly
- `offline` is also registered with the broker as the MQTT *last will*, so the broker publishes it if ANPR2MQTT crashes, is killed or loses its connection

While ANPR2MQTT is down, its entities show as *unavailable* in Home Assistant, rather than showing the last plate seen as if it were current. They come back once it reconnects.

Note

Before 1.2.0, entities kept their last state while ANPR2MQTT was down. Automations or dashboards that treat `unavailable` as an error may now see it during restarts and upgrades.

## Verifying it Works

Rather than wait for a container to need an update, you can check right away that Home Assistant has recognized the ANPR entities.

From the [Entities View](https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/configuration/entities_domains/), or the [Developer Tools](https://www.home-assistant.io/docs/tools/dev-tools/), filter the entities by `anpr.`

## Republishing on Home Assistant restart

Home Assistant's MQTT integration can publish the status of Home Assistant itself to *birth* and *last will and testament* topics. Current default for this is `homeassistant/status`, though older installations may have `hass/status` - if its non-default, override in the config under `homeassistant: status_topic`.

## Individual or Group Sensors

A single target, a group, or any mix of groups and targets, can be given an `entity_id` and published to Home Assistant as a sensor, with the state value being the last sighting timestamp, and the attributes being the combined history of the targets.

## More Home Assistant information

- [MQTT Integration](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/mqtt/)
  - Includes setting up a MQTT broker, MQTT Discovery, and trouble-shooting
- [MQTT Sensor](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/sensor.mqtt/)
- [MQTT Image](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/image.mqtt/)

# API

## DVLA

The United Kingdom's government free [Vehicle Enquiry Service (VES) API](https://developer-portal.driver-vehicle-licensing.api.gov.uk/apis/vehicle-enquiry-service/vehicle-enquiry-service-description.html) for licence lookup is supported directly.

Instructions for obtaining the required API Key and current URL are at the [DVLA Developer Portal](https://developer-portal.driver-vehicle-licensing.api.gov.uk), with the best place to start [Register For VES API](https://developer-portal.driver-vehicle-licensing.api.gov.uk/apis/vehicle-enquiry-service/vehicle-enquiry-service-description.html#register-for-ves-api). They also have a [Postman Collection](https://developer-portal.driver-vehicle-licensing.api.gov.uk/apis/vehicle-enquiry-service/assets/VES-API.postman_collection.json) for debugging and testing.

Configure the API key using the `DVLA__API_KEY` environment variable, the CLI argument, or in the configuration

```yaml
dvla:
    api_key: 59859j545h458957
    cache_ttl: 86400 # number of seconds to cache the result
    cache_type: FILE # cache implementation can be FILE or MEMORY
    cache_dir: /data/cache # where to store cached data if FILE chosen
    verify_plate: MAG1C # licence plate to check at startup to verify API and API Key working ok
```

### Example Response

```json
{
  "artEndDate": "2025-02-28",
  "co2Emissions" : 135,
  "colour" : "BLUE",
  "engineCapacity": 2494,
  "fuelType" : "PETROL",
  "make" : "ROVER",
  "markedForExport" : false,
  "monthOfFirstRegistration" : "2004-12",
  "motStatus" : "No details held by DVLA",
  "registrationNumber" : "ABC1234",
  "revenueWeight" : 1640,
  "taxDueDate" : "2007-01-01",
  "taxStatus" : "Untaxed",
  "typeApproval" : "N1",
  "wheelplan" : "NON STANDARD",
  "yearOfManufacture" : 2004,
  "euroStatus": "EURO 6 AD",
  "realDrivingEmissions": "1",
  "dateOfLastV5CIssued": "2016-12-25"
}
```

# Debug Tools

ANPR2MQTT ships an `anprtools` CLI with subcommands to help debug file system integration or OCR. All options can also be discovered via `--help`:

NOTE: if running from a checked out `anpr2mqtt` project with active `venv`, use `uv run anprtools ...` instead of `uvx --from anpr2mqtt anprtools ...` to run against your local checkout rather than the published package.

```bash
uvx --from anpr2mqtt anprtools --help
uvx --from anpr2mqtt anprtools ocr_file --help
uvx --from anpr2mqtt anprtools list_dir --help
```

## OCR (`ocr_file`)

Loads an image, runs OCR on it (with optional crop and invert), and prints the result. It ignores any YAML config file but respects environment variables. Useful for iterating quickly on bounding-box settings against a local image.

NOTE: OCR needs the [tesseract-ocr](https://github.com/tesseract-ocr/tesseract) binary on your `PATH`, which isn't installed by `uv`/`uvx`. The Docker image includes it, but to run outside Docker install it first, e.g. `brew install tesseract` on macOS or `apt install tesseract-ocr-eng` on Debian/Ubuntu. Without it, `ocr_file` reports `tesseract is not installed or it's not in your PATH` instead of an OCR result.

```bash
uvx --from anpr2mqtt anprtools ocr_file 20241230152519495_N74DYX_VEHICLE_DETECTION.jpg
```

All `event` and `ocr` settings can be overridden from the command line:

```bash
uvx --from anpr2mqtt anprtools ocr_file fixtures/20250602103045407_B4DM3N_VEHICLE_DETECTION.jpg \
  --ocr.crop.x 850 --ocr.crop.y 0 --ocr.crop.h 200 --ocr.crop.w 400 \
  --ocr.invert False
```

Key flags for `ocr_file`:

| Flag                    | Description                                 | Default           |
| ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `IMAGE_FILE`            | Image filename (positional)                 | required          |
| `--event.watch_path`    | Directory containing the image              | `.` (current dir) |
| `--event.image_name_re` | Regex to parse filename for plate/timestamp | Hikvision default |
| `--ocr.crop.x/y/h/w`    | Crop box coordinates and size (pixels)      | —                 |
| `--ocr.invert`          | Invert colours before OCR                   | `True`            |
| `--log_level`           | Logging verbosity                           | `INFO`            |

If no `event` config is defined, the image is looked for in the current working directory.

## Directory Listing (`list_dir`)

Lists images in a directory that match the ANPR image regular expression.

```bash
uvx --from anpr2mqtt anprtools list_dir
```

Override any `event` setting from the command line, for example to test a different path or regex, or events other than plates with `--event.target_type`:

```bash
uv run anprtools list_dir \
  --event.watch_path /ftp/Driveway \
  --event.image_name_re '(?P<dt>[0-9]{17})_(?P<target>[A-Z0-9]+)_(?P<event>VEHICLE_DETECTION)\.(?P<ext>jpg|png|gif|jpeg)'
```

Key flags for `list_dir`:

| Flag                    | Description                                                                                                                                    | Default           |
| ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `--event.watch_path`    | Directory to list                                                                                                                              | `.` (current dir) |
| `--event.image_name_re` | Regex to match filenames                                                                                                                       | Hikvision default |
| `--event.target_type`   | `plate`, or another type, such as `face`, for an `image_name_re` without a `target` group, listing each file's event name instead of its plate | `plate`           |
| `--log_level`           | Logging verbosity                                                                                                                              | `INFO`            |

## DVLA Lookup (`dvla_lookup`)

Performs a live DVLA vehicle enquiry for a registration plate and prints the JSON response. Useful for verifying your API key and checking what data the API returns for a given plate.

```bash
uvx --from anpr2mqtt anprtools dvla_lookup AB12CDE --dvla.api_key YOUR_API_KEY
```

The API key can also be supplied via the `DVLA__API_KEY` environment variable:

```bash
DVLA__API_KEY=your-key uv run anprtools dvla_lookup AB12CDE
```

Use `--test` to hit the DVLA UAT environment instead of production:

```bash
uvx --from anpr2mqtt anprtools dvla_lookup AB12CDE --dvla.api_key YOUR_KEY --test true
```

Key flags for `dvla_lookup`:

| Flag                | Description                              | Default       |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `REGISTRATION`      | Vehicle registration number (positional) | required      |
| `--dvla.api_key`    | DVLA API key                             | —             |
| `--dvla.cache_ttl`  | Cache TTL in seconds                     | `86400`       |
| `--dvla.cache_type` | Cache type                               | `FILE`        |
| `--dvla.cache_dir`  | Caching directory                        | `/data/cache` |
| `--test`            | Use UAT environment                      | `False`       |
| `--log_level`       | Logging verbosity                        | `INFO`        |

## Healthcheck (`healthcheck`)

Reports whether ANPR2MQTT is running and connected to MQTT. While it is, the main loop touches a heartbeat file every 10 seconds, and `healthcheck` exits non-zero if that file is missing or older than `--max_age` seconds (default 60). The Docker image runs it as its `HEALTHCHECK`, so `docker ps` shows the container as `healthy` or `unhealthy` with no extra configuration.

```bash
docker exec anpr2mqtt anprtools healthcheck
```

The heartbeat file is `anpr2mqtt.heartbeat` in the system temporary directory (`/tmp` in the container), or the path in the `ANPR2MQTT_HEARTBEAT_FILE` environment variable, which must be set the same for both the app and the healthcheck.

# Maximal Configuration

More extensive example configuration, using all the features

```yaml
---
log_level: DEBUG

events:
- camera: driveway
  event: anpr
  target_type: plate
  description: Vehicle identified at driveway camera
  watch_path: /ftp/Driveway
  image_name_re: (?P<dt>[0-9]{17})_(?P<target>[A-Z0-9]+)_(?P<event>VEHICLE_DETECTION)\.(?P<ext>jpg|png|gif|jpeg)
  image_url_base: http://192.168.10.10/CCTV
  auto_match_tolerance: 2
  ocr_field_ids:
    - hik_direction
- camera: driveway
  event: face
  description: Face seen at driveway camera
  target_type: face
  default_description: Face
  icon: mdi:face-recognition
  watch_path: /ftp/Driveway
  image_name_re: (?P<ip>[0-9.]+)_(?P<channel>[0-9]+)_(?P<dt>[0-9]{17})_(?P<event>FACE_SNAP|FACE_BACKGROUND)\.(?P<ext>jpg|png|gif|jpeg)
  secondary_image_event: FACE_BACKGROUND
  ocr_field_ids: []
- camera: shed
  event: line_crossing
  target_type: line_crossing
  watch_path: /ftp/shedcam
  description: Entry to back garden gate
  image_name_re: (?P<dt>[0-9]{17})_(?P<target>[A-Z0-9]+)_(?P<event>LINE_CROSSING)\.(?P<ext>jpg|png|gif|jpeg)
  image_url_base: http://192.168.10.10/CCTV
  autoclear:
    post_event: 360
    state: True
    image: False
- target_type: upload
  id: all
  description: All ftp uploads
  watch_path: /ftp
  watch_tree: true

cameras:
- name: driveway
  area: Driveway
  live_url: http://frigate.local/driveway
- name: shed
  area: back_garden
mqtt:
  host: 192.168.1.100
  port: 1883
  user: anpr2mqtt
  password: topsecret901
  topic_root: anpr2mqtt
  client_id: anpr2mqtt
homeassistant:
  discovery_topic_root: homeassistant
  device_creation: true
ocr:
  hik_direction:
    label: vehicle_direction
    values: Reverse, Forward
    invert: true
    crop: 
      x: 0
      y: 850
      h: 30
      w: 650
    correction:
      Forward:
      - F.*wd
      Reverse:
      - R.*v.*se
      - Back.*
image:
  jpeg_opts:
    quality: 30
    progressive: true
    optimize: true
  png_opts:
    quality: 30
    dpi: "(60, 90)"
    optimize: true
tracker:
  data_dir: /data

frigate:
    enabled: true
    topic: 
     - frigate/events
     - frigate//tracked_object_update
    min_score: 0.70
    url: http://frigate.local:5000
    cameras: 
      - driveway
      - garage

dvla:
  cache_ttl: 86400
  cache_type: file
  cache_dir: /data/cache
  api_key: MY6676SECRET787KEY
targets:
  plate:
    icon: mdi:car
    groups:
     - name: known
       members:
        - id: TJ912UKL
          description: joe's mini conv
          icon: mdi:car-convertible
          entity_id: my_summer_car
          correction:
            - J912UKL
            - TJ91.KL
        - id: P001PAT
          description: Postman
        - id: MY13CAR
          entity_id: my_truck
          description: Homeowner's old pickup
     - name: Amazon Prime
       entity_id: delivery_vehicle
       icon: "mdi:truck-delivery"
       members:
        - AM40PRM
     - name: dangerous
       priority: critical
       members:
         - id: B4DM3N
           description: Rural watch reported vehicle
    correction:
      UN001TST:
        - UN\d+1TST
        - UN001TSK
    ignore:
      - ^I\dZ$ # mis-read of tanker logo
```

# Minimal Configuration

Smallest working configuration ( although the actual smallest is no file at all and using only environment variables for MQTT )

```yaml
---
events:
  - target_type: plate
    watch_path: /ftp/hikcam2
mqtt:
  user: anpr2mqtt
  password: my_secret_password
  # assumes mqtt broker on localhost
```

# Docker Compose

Example Docker Compose configuration to run *ANPR2MQTT* as a container. This also requires a [.env](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk/examples/env/index.md), or alternatively adding the environment variables directly into the compose file.

```yaml
services:
  anpr2mqtt:
    container_name: anpr2mqtt
    image: ghcr.io/rhizomatics/anpr2mqtt:release
    volumes:
      - ./config:/config  # Config file lives at /config/anpr2mqtt.yaml inside the container
      - ./data/:/data     # Tracking data with JSON per plate recording visits, and DVLA cache
      - ./ftp:/media/cctv/ftp/driveway  # Example ftp landing zone
    restart: always
    env_file: ./.env  # Optional environment variables file
```

# Environment File

Example `.env` file for Docker Compose configuration to separately store the environment variables.

```bash
# Example env file for docker-compose.yaml

# To use these, add to config.yaml like ${oc.env:MQTT__HOST}

MQTT__HOST=192.168.0.1
MQTT__PORT=1883
MQTT__USER=my_mqtt_user
MQTT__PASS=my_mqtt_secret
```

# Home Assistant Automation

Example Home Assistant automation to send notifications when an MQTT update is received.

This uses [Supernotify](https://supernotify.rhizomatics.org.uk) to respect priorities and make multiple notifications for the same event - in the live example this includes Mobile Push alerts, email (with the snapshot ANPR image as an attachment), chimes ( hunting horn for known vehicles, doorbell chimes for unknown ) and Alexa spoken announcements.

It can be adapted to a plain notification by removing the `data` section and changing the `action`. Modern Home Assistant UI allows pasting in yaml to create automations.

```yaml
alias: Driveway ANPR Alert
description: Notify via email, chime, Alexa and mobile push when a vehicle identified
triggers:
  - trigger: state
    entity_id:
      - sensor.anpr_driveway
    attribute: event_time
conditions:
  - condition: not
    conditions:
      - condition: state
        entity_id: sensor.anpr_driveway
        state:
          - unavailable
          - unknown
actions:
  - action: notify.supernotifier
    metadata: {}
    data:
      message: >-
        {{ trigger.to_state.attributes.description }} with {{
        trigger.to_state.attributes.plate }} spotted at {{
        trigger.to_state.attributes.camera }} camera{% if
        trigger.to_state.attributes.vehicle_direction is defined %}, moving {{
        trigger.to_state.attributes.vehicle_direction }}{% endif %}

        {% if trigger.to_state.attributes.history.previous_sightings == 0 %} Not
        previously sighted  {% else %}  with {{
        trigger.to_state.attributes.history.previous_sightings }} previous
        sightings. {% endif %} {% if
        trigger.to_state.attributes.history.last_seen is defined and
        trigger.to_state.attributes.history.last_seen is not none %} last
        seen on {{ trigger.to_state.attributes.history.last_seen[:10] }} at
        {{ trigger.to_state.attributes.history.last_seen[11:16] }}   {%
        endif %}

        {% if 'reg_info' in trigger.to_state.attributes and
        trigger.to_state.attributes.reg_info is not none %}  DVLA info: {{
        trigger.to_state.attributes.reg_info }}   {% endif %}

        {% if 'hourly_counts' in trigger.to_state.attributes.history and
        trigger.to_state.attributes.history.hourly_counts is not none %}  Visit
        History: {% for time,count in
        trigger.to_state.attributes.history.hourly_counts.items() %}
          {{ time }}{% if int(time) < 12 %}am{% else %}pm{% endif %} : {{ count }} times
        {% endfor %}{% endif %}
      title: >-
        {{ trigger.to_state.attributes.description }} spotted on {{
        trigger.to_state.attributes.camera }} camera
      data:
        priority: "{{ trigger.to_state.attributes.priority }}"
        spoken_message: >-
          {{ trigger.to_state.attributes.description }} with {{
          trigger.to_state.attributes.plate }} spotted at {{
          trigger.to_state.attributes.camera }} camera{% if
          trigger.to_state.attributes.vehicle_direction is defined %}, moving {{
          trigger.to_state.attributes.vehicle_direction }}{% endif %}
        apply_scenarios: >-
          {% if trigger.to_state.attributes.known %}known_vehicle{% else
          %}unknown_vehicle{% endif %}
        constrain_scenarios:
          - known_vehicle
          - unknown_vehicle
        media:
          camera_entity_id: image.anpr_{{trigger.to_state.attributes.camera}}
          snapshot_url: >-
            {% if 'event_image_url' in trigger.to_state.attributes %}{{
            trigger.to_state.attributes.event_image_url }}{% endif %}
mode: single
```
# Developer

# Development Setup

## First Time

```bash
# Install uv
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

# Sync dependencies
uv sync

# Run the app
uv run anpr2mqtt
```

## Common Commands

```bash
# Install/sync dependencies
uv sync                    # Install all dependencies
uv sync --no-dev          # Production only (no dev dependencies)
uv sync --frozen          # Use lockfile without updating

# Run commands
uv run anpr2mqtt          # Run the application
uv run pytest             # Run tests
uv run python script.py   # Run any Python script

# Manage dependencies
uv add niquests           # Add production dependency
uv add --dev pytest       # Add dev dependency
uv remove package-name    # Remove a dependency
uv lock                   # Update lockfile after manual pyproject.toml edits

# Python version management
uv python install 3.14    # Install Python 3.14
uv python list            # List installed Python versions
uv venv                   # Create virtual environment
```

### Pre-commit Hooks

This project uses pre-commit hooks, run with [prek](https://prek.j178.dev) from `mise.toml`:

```bash
prek install
prek run --all-files
```

## Docker Build

```bash
# Build image
docker build -t anpr2mqtt .

# Run container
docker run -d \
  --restart always \
  -v /path/to/ftp:/ftp \
  -e MQTT_HOST=192.100.10.20 \
  -e MQTT_PORT=1883 \
  -e MQTT_USER=user \
  -e MQTT_PASS=pass \
  anpr2mqtt
```

## Dependencies Troubleshooting

### Need to regenerate lockfile?

```bash
rm uv.lock
uv lock
```

### Lockfile out of sync?

```bash
uv lock --upgrade  # Update all packages
uv sync --frozen   # Use exact lockfile versions
```

# Roadmap

No major changes are planned for ANPR2MQTT

## Minor Changes

- Auto cleanup of `requests-cache` objects once `niquests-cache` has been through a few releases

# Reference

# 1.4.2

## ✨ Enhancements

- Upload sensors have a `current` count, and `current_bytes`, of the files in the `watch_path` now, found by a scan at startup and each midnight, and kept up to date as files come and go, since the arrival counts, only from when watching started, could look like an empty directory
- Files removed from an upload's `watch_path`, deleted, moved out or renamed to a name that no longer matches, are counted, as `removed_today`, `removed_this_week`, `removed_total`, `last_removed` and `last_removed_file`
- A file renamed to a matching name, such as from an ftp server's temporary upload name, counts as an upload
- Sizes in bytes alongside every count, such as `today_bytes` and `total_bytes`, for both uploads and events' `images` attribute

# 1.4.1

## ✨ Enhancements

- New `mqtt.client_id` setting, defaulting to `anpr2mqtt` as before, so more than one `anpr2mqtt` can run against the same broker without each one disconnecting the other
- New `upload` target type, counting every file arriving in its `watch_path`, as a Home Assistant sensor of the last upload with `today`, `this_week`, `total` and `last_file` attributes. Nothing is published for each file, so nothing is notified. Use it as a general purpose ftp landing zone monitor, or alongside a directory's other events, to check there's some activity, such as scene changes, even when no plates arrive. Uploads aren't tied to a camera, which is optional for them, and several are told apart by a new `id` setting, such as `sensor.upload_shed` for `id: shed`. See [Uploads](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk/camera/#uploads)

## 💥 Breaking changes

- An event's `images` attribute counts only its own images, as `images.today` rather than `images.event.today`. The `camera` and `all` counts are gone, replaced by `upload` events, which can count a camera's directory, or one shared by all cameras

# 1.4.0

## ✨ Enhancements

- Other camera events, such as face capture, scene change, line crossing or region entry, defined by configuration alone. Any `target_type` other than `plate` is published as a Home Assistant event entity rather than a sensor, so integrations that take anpr2mqtt sensors as plates, such as Camera AutoNotify, don't see them, and has no plate lookups or corrections. See [Other Events](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk/camera/#other-events)
- The `target` group in `image_name_re` is only required for plate events, since most other events have nothing but a timestamp in their image names
- `default_description` and `icon` default by `target_type`, `Unknown vehicle` and `mdi:car-back` for plates as before, otherwise from the event name and `mdi:cctv`
- `event` and `ocr_field_ids` default by `target_type` too, `anpr` and the Hikvision vehicle direction for plates as before, otherwise the `target_type` and no OCR, so an event other than plates doesn't get `anpr` in its topics and entity ids
- New `secondary_image_event` event setting, for a second image of the same capture, such as Hikvision's `FACE_BACKGROUND` alongside its `FACE_SNAP`, published as its own image entity rather than as another event
- New `min_event_gap_seconds` event setting, for events without a target, so several images of the same face a second or so apart are published as one event
- Image counts, an `images` attribute on each event's entities, with `today`, `this_week`, `total` and `last_received` for the event, its camera and overall, for health checks such as no images from a camera today. Every image received is counted, whether or not it's published, and counts are kept in the data directory across restarts. See [Image Counts](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk/homeassistant/#image-counts)
- Home Assistant entities no longer configured, such as for a removed event, are removed at startup, along with their retained state. Only this instance's own entities are touched, it's skipped if any event fails to start, and `homeassistant.remove_stale_entities: false` switches it off. See [Removing Entities](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk/homeassistant/#removing-entities)
- MQTT login diagnostics: the source of the MQTT password, such as environment variable or config file, is logged at startup, so an old env var overriding the config file is easier to spot

## 💥 Breaking changes

- An existing event with a `target_type` other than `plate` is now an event entity, and its old sensor is removed from Home Assistant. Automations using that sensor need to use the event entity instead

## 🔒 Security

- Plates from Frigate, which any client that can publish to the MQTT broker could forge, were used unchecked in sighting history file names, so a plate such as `../../x` could read and write JSON files outside the data directory. Plates, Frigate camera names and Frigate event ids are now checked before use, and any sighting history file must be inside the data directory

## 🐛 Bug fixes

- Camera names, and each event's `event`, `camera` and `target_type`, are checked at startup, and must be letters, digits, `_` or `-`, since a space, `/`, `.` or an MQTT wildcard in one broke its topics, Home Assistant discovery or file names
- MQTT v5 login rejections, such as EMQX's `Bad user name or password`, are now logged as invalid credentials. paho also reports these as a `Protocol error` disconnect, which is the same failure
- Frigate licence plates are only matched to plate events, where previously the first event configured for a camera was used
- The milliseconds in an image name's 17 digit timestamp were read as microseconds, so `event_time` and the sighting history were up to a second early, such as `10:30:45.000407` for `10:30:45.407`. Sightings recorded before upgrading keep their old times

## 📚 Documentation

- Docs and examples give every event a `target_type`, including `plate`. It still defaults to `plate`, for older configurations, but an event without it is a plate event, with a plate sensor, even on a camera with no ANPR

## 📝 Other changes

- `anprtools list_dir` works for events without a target, with `--event.target_type`, listing each file's event name
- `mise.toml` installs Tesseract, via conda-forge, so OCR tests run locally

# 1.3.2

## 🐛 Bug fixes

- Italian and French plate validation patterns corrected to `AA123AA` format, and rules renamed `ITALY_1994` and `FRANCE_2009` to match the year each format was introduced

## 📝 Other changes

- Rebuilt container image to use an astral.sh reproducible Python build
- Also fixes CVE-2026-5435 and CVE-2026-19499 although neither of these had no exploits in the app.
- Minor fixes for test readability

## 📚 Documentation

- Updated to reflect new recommendation to use [Camera AutoNotify](https://camera-autonotify.rhizomatics.org.uk) and that this is now recommended for Frigate enrichment rather than anpr2mqtt.

# 1.3.1

## 📝 Other changes

- Correct version number for release
- `niquests-cache` replaces `requests-cache`, also removes otherwise unnecessary `requests` dependency
- Existing `requests-cache` files will be ignored, so requests re-cached that would otherwise be within `ttl` first time round
- Cache file location logged at startup. Cache files are easily distinguished - 64 char hashes for `niquests-cache` vs 16 for `requests-cache`. The two can co-exist until old ones tidied up.

## 🐛 Bug fixes

- Fixed error in handling a DVLA API rejection

# 1.3.0

This version adds support for an upcoming [Camera AutoNotify](https://camera-autonotify.rhizomatics.org.uk/developer/design/rfcs/rfc0003_anpr2mqtt/) release that will support ANPR2MQTT. The changes may also be generally useful where this app used in conjunction with Frigate.

## ✨ Enhancements

- Home Assistant devices now have manufacturer `Rhizomatics` and model `anpr2mqtt`, so integrations building on anpr2mqtt, such as Camera AutoNotify, can recognise them for certain. The device identifier is unchanged, so existing devices are kept
- A camera's `live_url` is its device's configuration URL in Home Assistant, where it's an `http` or `https` address
- New `linked_cameras` camera setting, naming the same camera in other integrations, such as Frigate, UniFi Protect, Viseron or Blue Iris, keyed by the Home Assistant domain of each, `frigate`, `unifiprotect`, `viseron` or `blueiris`
- A Frigate camera named differently from the anpr2mqtt camera its plates should be published as can be linked by `linked_cameras.frigate`. Without it, the Frigate camera of the same name is used, as before
- Every state has a `linked_cameras` attribute, those set, and the Frigate camera matched by name while the Frigate listener is on, for integrations such as Camera AutoNotify that join sightings to the events of those cameras

# 1.2.2

## ✨ Enhancements

- Docker image now has a built-in `HEALTHCHECK`, using the new `anprtools healthcheck` command. It passes while the main loop is running and connected to MQTT, and needs no broker credentials
- The old `/app/healthcheck.sh` script is removed. It waited for a heartbeat ANPR2MQTT never published, so it always failed. Remove any `healthcheck:` that calls it from your compose file
- `mosquitto-clients` and `jq` are no longer installed in the image, reducing CVE exposure
- OCR is checked at startup against a bundled sample image, logging `Verified OCR` or an error, so a missing or broken Tesseract shows up immediately rather than as every field reading `Unknown`. Turn off with `ocr.verify_on_startup: false`

## 🐛 Bug fixes

- Fix OCR in the Docker image, broken since 1.2.0: the `tesseract` binary was no longer installed, only its English language data, so OCR fields such as `vehicle_direction` always came out as `Unknown`

## 📝 Other changes

- Image rebuild for Debian CVE fixes
- Base images are pinned by digest, and published images are scanned daily, rebuilding when a fix is available

# 1.2.1

## 🐛 Bug fixes

- Home Assistant target sensors (a target or group given an `entity_id`) now keep the same `unique_id` across restarts. Previously it was rebuilt from a randomised hash each time ANPR2MQTT started, so Home Assistant could add a new entity after each restart, with a `_2`, `_3` suffix, and leave the old one behind as no longer provided
- After upgrading, delete any leftover target sensors from Home Assistant's entity list, and rename the remaining one back to its original entity ID if it picked up a suffix
- Republishing discovery when Home Assistant restarts no longer blocks the MQTT connection for the jittered delay, which held up Frigate events and keepalives while it ran

# 1.2.0

## 🚨 Breaking changes

- `tools` CLI renamed to `anprtools`, to avoid clashing with other packages' commands

## ✨ Enhancements

- Home Assistant entities now report availability on MQTT broker, consistent with Updates2MQTT
- ANPR2MQTT publishes
  - `online` to `anpr2mqtt/availability` when it connects
  - `offline` when it shuts down
  - sets `offline` as its MQTT last will, so the broker publishes it if the service crashes or is killed
- Every discovery config includes this as its `availability_topic`
- **Behaviour change**: while ANPR2MQTT is down, its entities in Home Assistant show as *unavailable* rather than keeping their last state. They come back when it reconnects
- See [Home Assistant Integration](https://anpr2mqtt.rhizomatics.org.uk/homeassistant/#availability)
- MQTT subscriptions, to Home Assistant status and Frigate events, are now renewed after a reconnect to the broker. Previously a dropped connection silently stopped Frigate events and Home Assistant restart detection until ANPR2MQTT was restarted

## 📝 Other changes

- Shrink docker image by removing build tooling
- Docker images now security scanned
- Automated testing now covers Python 3.13, 3.14, 3.15

## 🐛 Bug fixes

- Fix healthcheck by including `jq` in image

# 1.1.5

## 📝 Other changes

- Change pydantic dependency to `pydantic-settings[yaml]` since it now won't automatically import `pyyaml` otherwise
- Docker image no longer sets `MQTT__HOST`, `MQTT__PORT` and `MQTT__TOPIC_ROOT` env vars, which silently overrode the same settings in the YAML config file
- Test that the Docker image builds and the app starts inside it

# 1.1.4

## 📝 Other changes

- Security Fixes
- Pillow upgraded to v13.0.0 to remediate multiple CVEs
- Build chain certificate update for eMudhra intermediate ca certs issue
- Container rebuilt with latest `uv` version for eMudhra issue

## 📚 Documentation

- Documentation updated to include new for `tesseract` install when running OCR tools outside of Docker

# 1.1.3

## 📝 Other changes

- Moved docs theme to MaterialX
- `anpr2mqtt` and `tools` now installed as a `uv` tools inside container

## 📚 Documentation

- Docs publish `llms.txt` / `llms-full.txt` and per-page Markdown links for AI agents

# 1.1.2

## ✨ Enhancements

### Frigate Integration

- Populate `event_image_url` with snapshot for payload compatibility with file system detected images

## 🐛 Bug fixes

### Example Home Assistant Integration

- Fixed use of `vehicle_direction` and `history.last_sighting`

## 📝 Other changes

- Dependency refresh
- Documentation site build switched from `mkdocs` to `properdocs`

# 1.1.1

## Diagnostics

- When a message is republished because of HA restart or other event, this will be included as the `trigger` in the payload
- Reduced noisy INFO logging for non-LPR Frigate events

# 1.1.0

## Frigate Integration

- Optionally listen on MQTT for LPR detections in Frigate, and apply the same encrichment (DVLA, known plates) and corrections as for plates found via file system

## Auto-correction

- A recent plate with successful DVLA match will be used as a matching candidate for plates with poor match
- Dupe messages reduced, and spurious visit counting, by a minimum time gap
- Auto correct for common alpha/digit swaps by OCRs, with built-in rules for recent UK,French and Italian registrations

# 1.0.0

## Known Targets Configuration

- Restructured from 2 fixed groups ("known" and "dangerous") to a flexible groups structure, so any number of groups can be created, for example "family","postman","delivery","utility"
- Groups can have an `icon`,`entity_id` and `priority`, targets will inherit these if they don't have their own, or leave empty at group level and populate only on group members
- Existing config using `known` or `dangerous` will be translated at runtime to new structure
- `correction` lists of patterns or strings can now be added directly to target
- API lookup can be configured at target or group level, defaults to off, since vehicles already known

## Fuzzy Matching

- Close matches can be automatically matched to a known plate, with configurable tolerance
- `auto_match_tolerance` on Event config controls how far apart it can be, for example 1 or 2 different/missing/extra characters
  - Internally uses `rapidfuzz` with Levenshtein algorithm
  - Removes many cases for regular expressions, although still possible to provide them, or known bad readings as fixed strings

## Target specific sensors in Home Assistant

- Groups and individual targets can be given an `entity_id` and a sensor will be created in Home Assistant using MQTT discovery
- State for the sensor will be timestamp of last sighting, and combined past history will be attributes
- Any number of vehicles can be combined in a single sensor, so for example see last post vehicle detected, even if several come to the property
- Targets can now be more than a simple string - currently `description` and `entity_id` supported

## Time Analysis

- Previous sightings now have a richer set of analysis, with histogram data by visit hour of day, earliest/latest times

## Home Assistant

- Improved example automation
- Icon now configurable in the Event config, previously fixed at `mdi:car-back`

## Descriptions

- DVLA API client can now generate a description for unknown vehicles using the colour and vehicle make
- A `default_description` can be set on the Event config as a backup so there's never a null value passed to Home Assistant
- This defaults to "Unknown vehicle" however can be changed for other languages, or if being used for face/line-crossing detection

## Internals and Fixes

- Corrected example configurations
- Refactored internally to a `Sighting` class and a more complete `Target` definition, replacing ad hoc dicts

# 0.10.2

- Improve error handling when started without config file
- Fix healthcheck script use of MQTT env vars

# 0.10.1

- Update Home Assistant example to display a history summary, use the new `spoken_message` feature of Supernotify, and check `event_image_url` existing
- Now warns at start up if `image_base_url` has a trailing slash
- Always send a `history` value, defaulting to empty dict, to simplify HA templates
- Added pypi publishing

# 0.10.0

- Auto match plates with potential errors to known plates, using Levenshtein algorithm, and controlled via new `auto_match_tolerance` setting
- Historical analysis now provides a count of times vehicle previously seen by hour of the day, the earliest and latest time of day ever seen, and if the current visit is within that range

# 0.9.2

# 0.9.1

- Report % saved on image compression
- Option to specify a `verify_plate` to check the DVLA API at startup

# 0.9.0

- Settings now has configuration for `cache_dir` and to choose `cache_type` between `FILE` or `MEMORY`
- Add DVLA lookup to the CLI tools
- `uv run --with anpr2mqtt tools dvla_lookup MAG1C --dvla.api_key <my_api_key>`
  - (can skip the `--with anpr2mqtt` if running from checked out dir)

# 0.8.0

- Validate all regular expressions at startup

# 0.7.2

# 0.7.1

## Home Assistant Integration

- Now subscribes to the HA 'birth' and 'last will' messages to re-publish on HA restart
- State always published at startup
- Camera settings can be added, to add `area` and `live_url` to the message
- Camera Entity can now be added, and option to switch this and/or the Image entity creation

## Directory Scanning

- `watch_tree` can be set to recursively watch all subdirectories below `watch_path`

## MQTT

- MQTT protocol can now be set up to v5 or down to v3, defaults to v3.11

# 0.6.2

- For example, `vehicle_direction` could have different bounding boxes, or even values, on different cameras
- Suggested area provided for Home Assistant Device if configured
